clue.text: Vessel eagerly sought by reporters

definitions.meaning: a ladle or deep spoon used for serving is a kind of vessel
an exclusive story that a newspaper gets before its rivals

explanation.definitionFit: A ladle-like container is one sense; an exclusive news story beaten to print ahead of rivals is the journalistic sense.

clue.text: Poor Scots haul this old commentator

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and must be rearranged

parts.note: Scots as written plus haul, which the setter meant as hail so the letters match

explanation.surface: Badly done Scottish dragging, perhaps, describes a scholar of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' signals an anagram, but SCOTS HAUL lacks the I the answer needs and has a U it does not: the printed 'haul' should be 'hail'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholiast was an ancient or medieval scholar who wrote marginal notes explaining classical texts.

clue.text: Alternatively nip up to the plant

parts.note: or is the word offering an alternative

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word nip is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Suggests otherwise dashing up to the plant nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NIP to PIN in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpine is a succulent stonecrop, also called livelong, with purple flowers.

clue.text: Publicity for a formal proposal

parts.note: pro is Latin for in favour of
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting for debate

explanation.surface: A request for advertising to back a resolution at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is the marketing and advertising work that raises a product's profile.

clue.text: Trial undergone by Gulliver? Pish!

parts.note: the letters of this exclamation are those of a seagoing vessel, wrecked, that is jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses with a 'Pish!' the ordeals of Swift's traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: PISH is what you get when you take SHIP and WRECK it, so the instruction that builds the clue word is the answer. Gulliver's voyages each began with disaster at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulliver's adventures in Lilliput begin when his vessel founders and he is cast ashore, a calamity at sea.

clue.text: In this, a race naturally included an old Arab

indicators.note: included signals the answer sits within the run of words this, a race naturally

explanation.surface: Suggests that in some contest a running event was naturally part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' marks the letters inside 'thiS A RACE Naturally'; 'In' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for an Arab or Muslim, especially during the Crusades.

clue.text: In drink I'd appear lacking in taste

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls
the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: Someone worries they would seem dull after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food is bland, with little or no flavour.

clue.text: A strange brew 'e composed

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd by being rearranged

parts.note: the dropped-aitch form of he, giving just the letter E

explanation.surface: A Cockney says a man wrote an odd concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges BREW plus E; the whole clue also describes the composer, who wrote the opera Der Freischütz.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Maria von Weber was a German Romantic composer of operas, famous for a work on magic bullets.

clue.text: Heavenly creature in vice shake-up, spreading good news

indicators.note: in means the heavenly being is placed inside the reworked letters
a shake-up jumbles the letters of the word vice

parts.note: an angel is a heavenly being

explanation.surface: An angel stirs up a crackdown on sin while preaching the gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shake-up' scrambles the sin to EVIC, and 'in' sets the heavenly being inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic means relating to preaching the gospel, from Greek for good tidings.

clue.text: Whip for nothing, some might say

indicators.note: some might say means certain speakers pronounce it so, a sound-alike

parts.note: nowt is northern English dialect for nothing

explanation.surface: Suggests a lashing given for no reason at all.
explanation.walkthrough: NOWT is Northern English for nothing; the answer is often pronounced just like it, as 'some might say' hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout was a leather scourge formerly used for flogging in Russia.

clue.text: Cordial note from a Greek physician

indicators.note: from here means taken away out of the physician's name that follows

parts.note: Hippocrates, the ancient Greek father of medicine
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A doctor of ancient Greece writes a note prescribing a tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' means remove: TE taken out of HIPPOCRATES leaves the spiced wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocras was a medieval spiced and sweetened wine drunk as a restorative cordial.

clue.text: Hired assassin's transport to a centre of revolt

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the former national railway

indicators.note: centre of picks out the two middle letters of the word revolt

explanation.surface: A paid killer travels to where an uprising is taking place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes VO, the middle two letters of 'revolt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bravo is an old word, from Italian, for a hired thug or cut-throat.

clue.text: Language identified by many in turn

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, standing for a large number
a go is someone's turn in a game

explanation.surface: A tongue is recognised by a crowd taking it in turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal slang for a foreign tongue or specialist jargon.

clue.text: Fly like Wilbur, say, for protection of bookmakers

indicators.note: say means the phrase is pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to fly like Wilbur is to imitate (copy) Wilbur Wright, the aviation pioneer

explanation.surface: Flying like an aviation pioneer is somehow linked to safeguarding betting shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmakers' here is authors, people who make books, not betting firms. COPY WRIGHT, imitate Wilbur Wright, sounds the same as the answer, as 'say' indicates.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal ownership of a written work protects its authors from others reproducing it.

clue.text: This sale is universal indeed!

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another, here the letter for universal within the deed

parts.note: a deed is an action
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a sale is open to absolutely everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits into 'in deed': U goes inside ACTION. U is the British film certificate for 'universal', suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Sue a count for laceration of the skin

indicators.note: laceration means tearing, so the words are ripped apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman is taken to court over a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laceration' rearranges SUE A COUNT; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutaneous is the medical adjective for anything relating to the outer covering of the body.

clue.text: Reveal characters in vile dug out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Disclose what was found in a nasty excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of VILE DUG; 'characters in' just says those letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To divulge is to make known something secret, to disclose it.

clue.text: Truthful girl, about financial undertakings

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
c is short for circa, Latin for about
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: An honest young woman keeps track of her money matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracious means habitually honest, speaking the truth.

clue.text: See about revising rental forever

indicators.note: about means the cathedral city wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in England

indicators.note: revising means altering the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A tenant is told to look at changing the rent agreement for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revising' makes TERNAL, and 'about' wraps the see round it. A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means for all time, without end.

clue.text: Like Hyperion, she was once at sea

definitions.meaning: Hyperion was one of the Titans of Greek myth, so this means belonging to that race of giants
the famous liner that sank in 1912, a ship referred to as she

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the giant gods of Greek myth such as Hyperion, and it was also the name of the doomed White Star liner.

clue.text: Ravines, oriental, as are these types

parts.note: a chine is a deep narrow ravine, especially in southern England
E stands for east, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: Gorges in the Far East, much like these printed characters.
explanation.walkthrough: A chine is a steep ravine on the coasts of Dorset and the Isle of Wight. The definition refers to written characters of a script.
explanation.definitionFit: The written characters of the language of China are a kind of type or script.

clue.text: Aboard which many go to Delphi?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral one hundred, used for many
Delphi was the site of the most famous oracle of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: Asks what crowds of pilgrims travel in on their way to consult the Greek seer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the vessel one travels 'aboard'; 'go to' joins C and the oracle at Delphi.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat of wicker and hide, so it is something one sits in on the water.

clue.text: Plant a money-making concern under Tom

indicators.note: under puts the mint below the tom in this down clue

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
the Mint is where coins are produced

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a profitable business below a man named Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' places MINT below CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint, or catnip, is an aromatic herb whose scent attracts cats.

clue.text: Study the text of "The Reluctant Warrior"

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a script is the written text of a play or film

explanation.surface: Reads like a direction to go over the screenplay of a war film.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title looks like a film to study, but it is the definition: a soldier called up against his will.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is compelled into military service, so is often an unwilling soldier.

clue.text: Genoese navigator or retired seaman

definitions.meaning: John (Giovanni) ..., the Italian explorer who sailed for England to North America in 1497
read cryptically as AB (able seaman) gone to bed, inside a COT

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a seaman (AB) who has retired, gone to bed, is in a COT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian-naturalised Genoese explorer sailed for England, and a sailor tucked into a small bed spells out the same name.

clue.text: In unconscious state we see many such butterflies

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but it means one of that species

indicators.note: In means the letter for many goes inside the state of unconsciousness

parts.note: a coma is a state of deep unconsciousness
M is the Roman numeral one thousand, used for many

explanation.surface: A patient in a coma sees swarms of butterflies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts M inside COMA; 'we see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The comma is a species of butterfly named for the white mark on its underwing shaped like a punctuation mark.

clue.text: Sovereign emblem of victory

definitions.meaning: the monarch, or royal power, is referred to by the regal headgear
a wreath of laurel placed on a winner's head

explanation.definitionFit: The word stands for the monarch or royal authority, and also for the laurel wreath awarded to a victor.

clue.text: College recess

definitions.meaning: one of the colleges of Oxford University
a bay window projecting from an upper storey, forming an alcove

explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of an Oxford college and of a projecting bay window forming an alcove in a room.

clue.text: It's used to clean up the plant

definitions.meaning: a brush with a long handle for sweeping floors
a yellow-flowered shrub of heaths and hillsides

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the sweeping brush and the yellow-flowered shrub whose twigs were once bound to make such brushes.

clue.text: Organized riot, ideal for this leader

indicators.note: organized means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper item calls a planned disturbance the perfect thing for its political chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organized' rearranges RIOT IDEAL. 'leader' is the newspaper sense, a lead article giving the paper's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers the opinion column written by the editor is called the leading article.

clue.text: Will try Manet's sort

parts.note: to try something is to test it

indicators.note: sort used as a verb means arrange, so the painter's name is rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A curious request to sample the French painter's kind of picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' scrambles the painter's name into AMENT, placed after the word for try.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document setting out a person's bequests.

clue.text: Excursion for everyone in borders of Surrey

indicators.note: in places the word for everyone between the two edge letters
borders of picks the first and last letters of Surrey

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A trip out for all the family in the Surrey countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of' gives S and Y, the first and last letters of 'Surrey'; Surrey is a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a short outing or jaunt, as well as a sudden sortie from a besieged place.
